## Setup
```{r}
options(conflicts.policy = "depends.ok")
library(tidyverse)
plot_grid <- cowplot::plot_grid
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/format_path.R?raw=true")
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/fun_eda.R?raw=true")
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/fun_plots.R?raw=true")
#source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/study_llmpanel/blob/main/scripts/functions_llmpanel.R?raw=true")

path_processed <- format_path("llmpanel/data_processed")

# Read in and format full panel (wide)
panel <- format_eda(read_csv(
  here::here(path_processed, "panel.csv"),show_col_types = FALSE))
```

# Tone Preferences
```{r}
pref_means <- panel |> summarise(
  'Legitimizing' = mean(pref_legitimizing, na.rm = TRUE),
  'Norms' = mean(pref_norms, na.rm = TRUE),
  'Value Affirmation' = mean(pref_value_affirmation, na.rm = TRUE),
  'Self Efficacy' = mean(pref_self_efficacy, na.rm = TRUE),
  'Acknowledging' = mean(pref_acknowledging, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "tone", values_to = "mean_pref")

pref_means |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(tone, -mean_pref), y = mean_pref, fill = tone)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_pref, 2)), vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Tone", y = "Mean Preference")
```

```{r}
pref_long <- panel |>
  select(subid, pref_legitimizing, pref_norms, pref_value_affirmation,
         pref_self_efficacy, pref_acknowledging) |>
  pivot_longer(-subid, names_to = "tone", values_to = "pref") |>
  mutate(subid = factor(subid),
         tone = case_match(
    tone,
    "pref_legitimizing" ~ "Legitimizing",
    "pref_norms" ~ "Norms",
    "pref_value_affirmation" ~ "Value Affirmation",
    "pref_self_efficacy" ~ "Self Efficacy",
    "pref_acknowledging" ~ "Acknowledging"),
    tone = fct_reorder(tone, pref, mean, na.rm = TRUE))

pref_long |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tone, y = pref, fill = tone)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = \(d) d |>
      group_by(tone) |>
      filter(pref < quantile(pref, .25, na.rm = TRUE) - 1.5 * IQR(pref, na.rm = TRUE) |
               pref > quantile(pref, .75, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.5 * IQR(pref, na.rm = TRUE)),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.25, height = 0.05, seed = 123),
    alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 2, fill = "white") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "text",
               aes(label = round(after_stat(y), 2)), vjust = -1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  labs(x = "Tone", y = "Preference")
```

## Inferential Tests

Repeated-measures ANOVA: does mean preference differ across tones?

```{r}
aov_tone <- afex::aov_ez(
  id = "subid", dv = "pref", data = pref_long, within = "tone",
  anova_table = list(correction = "GG"))
aov_tone
```

Pairwise comparisons for the ANOVA (Holm-adjusted)

```{r}
emmeans::emmeans(aov_tone, pairwise ~ tone, adjust = "holm")
```

Friedman test (non-parametric check on the same question)

```{r}
friedman.test(pref ~ tone | subid, data = pref_long)
```

Pairwise comparisons for the Friedman test: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (Holm-adjusted)

```{r}
pref_complete <- pref_long |>
  group_by(subid) |>
  filter(!any(is.na(pref))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(tone, subid)

pairwise.wilcox.test(
  pref_complete$pref, pref_complete$tone,
  paired = TRUE, p.adjust.method = "holm", exact = FALSE)
```

### Takeaways

These findings provide support for the removal of value-affirmation and acknowledging tones, whose mean ratings are significantly lower than the top 3. Within the grouping of legitimizing, self-efficacy and norms tones we see support for utilizing these tones together for the potential benefits of variability in support messages across a long period.















*Pivot long format*

We'll retain a separate wide-format object to examine demographics etc.

```{r}
panel_long <- panel |>
  select(subid, dem_age:dem_minority, q1_legitimizing_1:q6_formality_1,
         `x1_hi_1_fl_1`:`x4_li_10_in_1`,
         -contains("timing"), -contains("attention")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols= `x1_hi_1_fl_1`:`x4_li_10_in_1`,
    values_to = "message_rating",
    names_to = "message_type") |>
  separate(message_type,
           sep = "_", into = c(
             "survey_version", "context", "q_num", "tone_style"),
           extra = "drop") |> 
  mutate(
    style = if_else(substr(tone_style, 1, 1) == "f", "formal", "informal"),
    tone = case_when(
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "l" ~ "legitimizing",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "n" ~ "norms",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "s" ~ "self_efficacy",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "a" ~ "acknowledging",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "v" ~ "value_affirmation"),
    context = case_when(
      context == "hi" ~ "high_increasing",
      context == "hd" ~ "high_decreasing",
      context == "li" ~ "low_increasing")
  ) |>
  select(-q_num, -tone_style) |> 
  filter(!is.na(message_rating),
         str_trim(message_rating) != "")

# Sanity-check that we have 30 rows per respondent
nrow(panel_wide)*30 == nrow(panel_long)
```


# Preferences by Demographic

`pref_test()` regresses each `pref_` column on a `dem_` column with `lm()`
(equivalent to a t-test for a two-level variable) and returns the coefficients and p-values.

```{r}
pref_test <- function(data, dem) {
  dem <- rlang::as_name(rlang::ensym(dem))

  data |>
    select(all_of(dem), starts_with("pref_")) |>
    pivot_longer(starts_with("pref_"), names_to = "pref", values_to = "value") |>
    nest(.by = pref) |>
    mutate(fit = map(data, \(d) broom::tidy(lm(reformulate(dem, "value"), data = d)))) |>
    select(pref, fit) |>
    unnest(fit) |>
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    select(pref, term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) |>
    arrange(p.value)
}

panel |> pref_test(dem_sex)
```

Run `pref_test()` across binary/numeric `dem_` columns and keep the significant tests.

```{r}
dem_cols <- str_subset(names(panel), "^dem_") |>
  setdiff(c("dem_income", "dem_education"))

all_tests <- dem_cols |>
  set_names() |>
  map(possibly(\(d) pref_test(panel, !!rlang::sym(d)), otherwise = NULL)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "dem") |>
  arrange(p.value)

sig_tests <- all_tests |>
  filter(p.value < .05) |>
  arrange(pref, p.value) |>
  select(-dem)
sig_tests
```

# Message Ratings by Tone

Each respondent rated several messages per tone, so ratings are first averaged within respondent and tone. The tests then mirror the preference analysis: a repeated-measures ANOVA and a Friedman test across the five tones, each followed by Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons.

```{r}
rating_levels <- c("strongly_disagree", "disagree", "somewhat_disagree", "neutral",
                   "somewhat_agree", "agree", "strongly_agree")

rating_by_tone <- panel_long |>
  mutate(rating_num = as.numeric(factor(message_rating, levels = rating_levels))) |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(subid, tone)) |>
  mutate(subid = factor(subid),
         tone = fct_reorder(tone, rating, mean, na.rm = TRUE))

rating_by_tone |> summarise(mean = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .by = tone) |> arrange(mean)
```

```{r}
aov_rating <- afex::aov_ez(
  id = "subid", dv = "rating", data = rating_by_tone, within = "tone",
  anova_table = list(correction = "GG"))
aov_rating

emmeans::emmeans(aov_rating, pairwise ~ tone, adjust = "holm")
```

```{r}
friedman.test(rating ~ tone | subid, data = rating_by_tone)

rating_complete <- rating_by_tone |>
  group_by(subid) |>
  filter(!any(is.na(rating))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(tone, subid)

pairwise.wilcox.test(
  rating_complete$rating, rating_complete$tone,
  paired = TRUE, p.adjust.method = "holm", exact = FALSE)
```
